records.rationale: The packet contains matching ClaimsPro and Snowflake header data, the phone FNOL transcript (call_excerpt.md), a one-page clinic summary (medical_summary.pdf), the adjuster notes (adjuster_notes.md) and three photos. The claimant's account of a rear impact and same-day neck and lower-back treatment matches the medical summary. The date of service on medical_summary.pdf is in a different typeface from the rest of the page. The scene photo IMG_0205.jpg shows leafless trees that do not fit the September 19 date of loss, and the insured vehicle photo IMG_0204.jpg shows rust along the damage edges. The medical charges on file total about $2,635, against a claimed $59,533.85, and nothing on file explains the difference. The police report, provider bill, exam notes, imaging and coverage verification are indexed in ClaimsPro but not on file, and policy status is unknown with blank policy dates. These documents and photos should be verified at source before a person relies on them; the claim also requires human review by regulation.
